name: Club Kit
description: Firm synthesized drum kit for house and dance music: twelve drums, one on each key of the octave, with a crash, a ride, congas and a cowbell among them, and the octave of the key tuning the drum.

params.name: Kit
params.description: The character of the whole kit: firm and tight, deep and round with a lower kick, dusty with worn gritty tops, or bright with the tops forward. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Tune
params.description: Tunes every drum up or down, the same way the octave of the key played does. At zero every pitched drum sits on a white key. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Length
params.description: How long every drum rings, from clipped taps to a long kick and long cymbal washes. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Punch
params.description: How far and how fast the kick and congas fall in pitch as they start, and how hard their first moments are. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Snap
params.description: The click on the kick, the noise on the snare, the slap on the congas and the bite at the front of the hats and cymbals, down to soft starts. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Dull to bright: a filter over the top of the tonal drums and the upper edge of the noise drums and cymbals. Dull also makes the hats, shaker and cymbals quieter.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Soft saturation over the whole kit: the kick stays about where it is and everything quieter comes up, so more of it is thicker and more even.

params.name: Variation
params.description: How much each hit differs from the last in level, tone, length, pitch and noise. At zero a drum repeats exactly, as a machine does. Heard from the next hit.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far the hats, cymbals, shaker, rim, congas and cowbell sit from the centre and how wide the crash and clap spread, down to mono. Kick and snare stay centred.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the kit. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many drums land together.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, beside the Drum Kit and on its plan of twelve keys and two slots a drum. Every drum is synthesized the way drum machine voices usually are (a swept sine through a waveshaper, filtered noise, banks of detuned pulses for the metal, pulse pairs through a band-pass); nothing is sampled and no circuit is modelled.
